dialogue.origin: (本日はよろしくお願いします。時間になりましたら始めさせていただきます）
dialogue.content: (Thank you for joining me today. We'll get started at the scheduled time.)

dialogue.origin: (かしこまりました。はい、どうぞよろしくお願いします。)
dialogue.content: (Understood. Yes, I'm ready when you are.)

dialogue.origin: こんばんは。本日はご相談ありがとうございます。お時間になりましたので、相談員からご連絡申し上げます。
dialogue.content: Good evening. Thank you for reaching out for a consultation today. It's time for our session to begin.

dialogue.origin: 今日はよろしくお願いいたします。差し支えない範囲で年齢と性別、ご相談内容をお話しください。
dialogue.content: I look forward to speaking with you. To start, could you please tell me your age, gender, and what you'd like to discuss, to the extent you're comfortable?

dialogue.origin: 中２、男です落ち込むともとに戻れなくなる性格を直したいので、方法を教えてほしいですよろしくお願いします
dialogue.content: I'm a second-year middle school student, a boy. I want to change the part of my personality where I can't bounce back after getting down, so I'd like you to tell me how. Thank you.

dialogue.origin: そうでしたか、お話ししてくれてありがとうございます。
dialogue.content: I see. Thank you for sharing that with me.

dialogue.origin: 「落ち込むと元に戻れなくなる」をもう少し具体的にお話しできますか？
dialogue.content: Could you tell me a little more specifically what you mean by "not being able to bounce back after getting down"?

dialogue.origin: 落ち込むと、人と話すのがうまくいかないことが多いです
dialogue.content: When I get down, I often have trouble talking with people.

dialogue.origin: なるほど。
dialogue.content: I see.

dialogue.origin: どのくらい落ち込むことがありますか？毎日、とか週に何回くらいとか？
dialogue.content: How often do you feel down? For instance, every day, or a few times a week?

dialogue.origin: 決まってはないです落ち込んだら、長くそのままもどれないです
dialogue.content: It's not on a set schedule. When I do get down, I can't get back to normal for a long time.

dialogue.origin: 長くもどれない、、落ち込むときってどんな時ですか？例えば、、とかでもいいですよ。
dialogue.content: A long time to get back to normal... When are the times you feel down? You can give me an example.

dialogue.origin: 色々なんですが、肌荒れがひどくなった時とかもあります
dialogue.content: It's various things, but for instance, it happens when my skin breaks out badly.

dialogue.origin: 肌荒れは、落ち込んだら肌が荒れるという理解で大丈夫ですか？
dialogue.content: Regarding the skin breakouts, am I understanding correctly that you feel down first, and then your skin breaks out?

dialogue.origin: いえ、肌が荒れてそれが気になって落ち込むということです
dialogue.content: No, it's that my skin breaks out, and I get self-conscious about it, which makes me feel down.

dialogue.origin: なるほど、ご確認ありがとうございます。肌荒れ（大変ですね）、そのほかに落ち込むきっかけとか思い出せますか？
dialogue.content: I see, thank you for clarifying. Skin breakouts (that must be tough)... can you think of any other things that trigger you to feel down?

dialogue.origin: あとは髪を理容室で切られすぎて、変な髪型になった時もです
dialogue.content: Also when they cut my hair too short at the barbershop and it looks strange.

dialogue.origin: 変な髪形、、期待通りにならなかったんですね、それは、残念な気持ちになりますね。
dialogue.content: A strange hairstyle... so it didn't turn out the way you'd hoped. That must be disappointing.

dialogue.origin: 落ち込んでいる間は、どんな風に過ごされていますか？学校で、とか、家で、とか。
dialogue.content: While you're feeling down, how do you usually spend your time? At school, or at home, for example.

dialogue.origin: 自信が無くなった感じになって、何も楽しめなくなるような状態です
dialogue.content: I feel like I've lost confidence, and I can't enjoy anything.

dialogue.origin: グループワークなどでも言いたいことも言えなくて、つらい感じです
dialogue.content: Even in group work, I can't say what I want to, and it feels painful.

dialogue.origin: 楽しい気持ちになれないんですね。それで、グループワークで、とか人とうまく話せなくなってしまうんですね。
dialogue.content: So you can't feel happy. And because of that, you find it hard to talk with people, like during group work.

dialogue.origin: つらいですね。
dialogue.content: That sounds tough.

dialogue.origin: 落ち込んだ期間はもう自分が自分じゃないほど、本当につらいところがあります
dialogue.content: When I'm down, there are times when it's so painful I don't even feel like myself anymore.

dialogue.origin: ここまでのお話だと、髪型や肌など、他の人から見えるところについて、がおちこむきっかけになっているように思えますが、
dialogue.content: From what you've told me so far, it seems that things others can see, like your hairstyle or your skin, are what triggers you to feel down.

dialogue.origin: 容姿以外でもすごく落ち込んで、「自分じゃない」みたいに感じたことはありますか？
dialogue.content: Have you ever felt extremely down and like you're "not yourself" over something other than your appearance?

dialogue.origin: きっかけになるのは見ためのことが多いと思いますそこでもっとつらくなるのは、そこからもとの見た目になるまでずっと落ち込みが直らないことです
dialogue.content: I think the trigger is usually my appearance. What makes it even harder is that the feeling doesn't go away until my appearance returns to normal.

dialogue.origin: なるほど、
dialogue.content: I see.

dialogue.origin: どうしたら気にしないで、元の通りに過ごせるのか教えてください
dialogue.content: Please tell me how I can stop worrying about it and just live normally.

dialogue.origin: 今日お話しすることを一緒に整理しましょうね
dialogue.content: Let's organize what we've discussed today together.

dialogue.origin: 容姿について気になることがあるとすごく落ち込んで、人と話したりできなくなる。それがとてもつらい。
dialogue.content: When something about your appearance bothers you, you get very down and it becomes hard to talk to people. That's very painful for you.

dialogue.origin: はい、そのとおりです
dialogue.content: Yes, that's exactly right.

dialogue.origin: 気にせず元の通りに過ごせるための方法を一緒に考える。ということで大丈夫ですか？
dialogue.content: So, we will think together about ways for you to live as you normally would without worrying. Does that sound right?

dialogue.origin: はい、その方法が知りたいです
dialogue.content: Yes, I want to know how to do that.

dialogue.origin: すごく前向きな相談でいいと思います。ご自身で課題をしっかり話してらっしゃいますね。
dialogue.content: I think this is a very proactive way to approach this. You're able to state your problem very clearly.

dialogue.origin: 落ち込むときというのは、誰かに髪型のことを指摘されたとか、きっかけがありましたか？
dialogue.content: When you feel down, is there a trigger, like someone pointing out your hairstyle?

dialogue.origin: 自分で鏡を見てです誰か言う人はいないです、弟らが少し言ってきますが
dialogue.content: It’s when I see myself in the mirror. No one really says anything, though my younger brothers make a few comments.

dialogue.origin: お兄さんなんですね。肌荒れの時もそうでしたか？
dialogue.content: So you're an older brother. Was it the same when your skin broke out?

dialogue.origin: はい、それはあります
dialogue.content: Yes, that happens.

dialogue.origin: 特に誰に言われたわけではないけれど、自分で気になって、自分に自信がなくなる、ということですかね
dialogue.content: So, even though no one in particular says anything, you become self-conscious about it and lose your confidence, is that right?

dialogue.origin: はい、そうです
dialogue.content: Yes, that's right.

dialogue.origin: マルコさんは、ご自身がどう見えるかについて、理想とかこうありたい　とか、ありますか？
dialogue.content: Marco, do you have an ideal, or a certain way you'd like to look?

dialogue.origin: 肌がきれいで、癖っ毛じゃない方が良いです
dialogue.content: I'd rather have clear skin and not have curly hair.

dialogue.origin: なるほど、マルコさんは癖っ毛？
dialogue.content: I see. Do you have curly hair, Marco?

dialogue.origin: 中学に入ってから、そうです
dialogue.content: Yes, ever since I started middle school.

dialogue.origin: 髪質は変わるんですね。なるほどなるほど、、たとえば、
dialogue.content: Hair texture can change, I see. I see... For example,

dialogue.origin: 相談員が中学生の時は、あまりに直毛なので、すこし癖のある友達がうらやましいね、なんて、直毛の友達とはなしたものですが、これを聞いて　どう思われますか？
dialogue.content: When I was in middle school, my hair was very straight, and I used to talk with my straight-haired friends about how we envied friends who had a bit of a wave. What do you think when you hear that?

dialogue.origin: 自分はただすごく嫌ですね
dialogue.content: For me, I just really hate it.

dialogue.origin: うん、うん、
dialogue.content: Mm‑hm, mm‑hm.

dialogue.origin: 質問を変えますね。マルコさんは、「自分が自分じゃないとおもうほどつらい」時、他の人がどうみてるか、とか考えていますか？
dialogue.content: Let me ask a different question. Marco, when you're feeling so pained that you "don't feel like yourself," are you thinking about how other people are seeing you?

dialogue.origin: それは思います
dialogue.content: Yes, I do think about that.

dialogue.origin: どんな風に　感じてますか？その時のマルコさんの感じてることを話せますか？
dialogue.content: How does that feel? Can you tell me what you're feeling at that time?

dialogue.origin: すみません、どの時の気持ちのことを話すといいですか？
dialogue.content: Sorry, which time's feelings should I talk about?

dialogue.origin: 質問の仕方が悪かったですね。言い直しますね
dialogue.content: My question wasn't very clear. Let me rephrase it.

dialogue.origin: 人がどう見ているかを考えて「自分が自分じゃない」ように感じているときのお気持ち　です
dialogue.content: It's the feeling you get when you're thinking about how others see you and you feel like you're "not yourself."

dialogue.origin: すみません、ちょっと分からないです
dialogue.content: Sorry, I don't quite understand.

dialogue.origin: 難しいですね、
dialogue.content: It is a difficult question.

dialogue.origin: では、人からどんなふうに思われている、と感じますか？例えば、髪型が変になったとき。
dialogue.content: Okay, then how do you feel people think of you? For example, when your hairstyle looks strange.

dialogue.origin: 切りすぎてて変だなぁとか、髪がうねってて変だなぁとか思われてると思います
dialogue.content: I think they're thinking things like, "It's cut too short and looks weird," or "His hair is wavy and strange."

dialogue.origin: うん、うん、
dialogue.content: Mm-hmm, I see.

dialogue.origin: 実際は、言われたことがない、ということでしたね？
dialogue.content: But in reality, no one has actually said that to you, is that right?

dialogue.origin: でもそこよりも、自分の思う通りの姿でない自分を外に出していかないといけない状態の方がつらいです
dialogue.content: But more than that, what's more painful is having to go out in public not looking the way I want to.

dialogue.origin: うん、うん、、
dialogue.content: Mm‑hm, mm‑hm...

dialogue.origin: 今までは、思い通りでない状態になっても、いつも通りに学校に行けてましたか？？
dialogue.content: Up until now, even when you didn't look the way you wanted, have you still been able to go to school as usual?

dialogue.origin: 行かないと親に行けと言われるので、行くしかないです
dialogue.content: If I don’t go, my parents tell me to go, so I have no choice but to go.

dialogue.origin: 行きたくない気持ちで、毎日行っています
dialogue.content: I go every day, feeling like I don't want to.

dialogue.origin: それでも、つらいきもちを乗り越えて、学校に行って、グループワークにも参加して、、たんですね。
dialogue.content: And yet, you've been pushing through those difficult feelings to go to school and even participate in group work.

dialogue.origin: そこまで大げさではないですでもつらいものはつらいとこがあります
dialogue.content: It's not that big of a deal. But what's painful is still painful.

dialogue.origin: それだけでも、ご自身の課題に向き合う一歩になっていると思います、相談員は。
dialogue.content: I believe that alone is a step toward facing your own challenge.

dialogue.origin: 髪型や、肌荒れ、に対しての嫌な気持ち、を減らすために、。マルコさんは、今まで試したこととかありますか？
dialogue.content: To reduce the negative feelings you have about your hairstyle and skin breakouts... Marco, is there anything you've tried so far?

dialogue.origin: 皮膚科にはちゃんと親に連れて行ってもらいます
dialogue.content: My parents make sure to take me to a dermatologist.

dialogue.origin: なるほど、肌荒れを治す。これはひとつの努力ですね。
dialogue.content: I see, so treating the skin condition. That's one thing you're doing.

dialogue.origin: 髪型そのものや、肌荒れそのものを何とかする、のは直接的なひとつのやり方でいいと思います。
dialogue.content: I think directly addressing the hairstyle itself or the skin issues is one good, direct approach.

dialogue.origin: もう一つは、髪型や肌荒れ、に対する、マルコさんの気持ちの持ち方も、ご自身を「自分じゃない」ほどのつらさに関係しているのかなと思うのですが、どう思いますか？
dialogue.content: Another aspect is the way you think about your hair or skin. I wonder if that's also connected to the painful feeling of being "not yourself." What are your thoughts on that?

dialogue.origin: 質問がむずかしいです、、
dialogue.content: That question is difficult...

dialogue.origin: 何度もすみません。
dialogue.content: I'm sorry for asking so many difficult questions.

dialogue.origin: 例えばですが、髪は伸びる、と考えると、マルコさんの髪が短い「今」のつらさには終わりがあると考えるとか。
dialogue.content: For example, if you consider that hair grows, you could think of the pain of your hair being short "now" as something that has an end.

dialogue.origin: なかなか気楽には考えられないです
dialogue.content: It's hard for me to think about it that casually.

dialogue.origin: 気楽、までいかなくても、追い詰めなくてもいいかな～くらいには、どうかな？
dialogue.content: Maybe not to the point of being casual, but what about just not being so hard on yourself about it? How does that sound?

dialogue.origin: 毎日毎日が気になってつらいのでむずかしいです
dialogue.content: It's difficult because I worry about it every single day, and it's painful.

dialogue.origin: そっか、毎日つらいんですね。マルコさんのお友達もそうだと思うんだけど、容姿がすごく大切に思える時期だとおもいます。でも、
dialogue.content: I see, so it's painful every day. I think for your friends too, this is an age where appearance feels very important. But,

dialogue.origin: 容姿が変わっても、人の中身は（マルコさんがどんな人物か）は変わらないと思います。日々成長はしていると思いますが。
dialogue.content: even if your appearance changes, who you are on the inside (the kind of person you are) doesn't change. Although I do believe you're growing every day.

dialogue.origin: これも難しいかな。
dialogue.content: Perhaps this is difficult too.

dialogue.origin: はい
dialogue.content: Yes.

dialogue.origin: そっか。難しいね。。
dialogue.content: I see. It’s hard, isn’t it.

dialogue.origin: 寝ないといけないので今日は終わりでお願いします
dialogue.content: I have to go to sleep, so can we please end for today?

dialogue.origin: また、ここに相談に来ていただいてもいいし、お友達とお話ししてみるのも一案だと思います。
dialogue.content: You are always welcome to come back here to talk, and talking with your friends might be another option to consider.

dialogue.origin: 遅くまでありがとう。
dialogue.content: Thank you for staying up late.

dialogue.origin: 終了メッセージを送ります。
dialogue.content: I will send the session-end message now.

topic.sub: 自尊心の低下と外見への過剰な不安
